items.title: Moksy's economics and its documented growth motion
items.body: Moksy's SEO document (written 21 September 2026) says Moksy costs £19 to £79 a month, so its revenue is a volume number: at those prices £100k a year is roughly 280 to 440 paying subscribers. It concludes that outbound sales cannot reach that and that growth "is a content and search problem". The documented motion is therefore guides and search, shipped at one guide a week, with two events to track by landing page: free Blueprint started and Pro upgrade. Results are reviewed at 4, 8 and 12 weeks along the chain impressions, clicks, Blueprints, Pro: a guide with impressions but no clicks needs a better title; one with clicks but no Blueprints needs a better close. Nothing should be expected for four to eight weeks, because judging earlier measures the crawler's schedule, not the content. Paid social is not part of the documented motion: any Facebook or Instagram test is new and has to earn its place against the same numbers. A subscriber on £19 a month pays £228 in a year before churn and costs, which sets a ceiling on what can sensibly be paid to win one. Source: moksy.ai docs/SEO.md.

questions.prompt: Design a 12-week paid Facebook test for Moksy that fits its documented economics and motion. State the objective, the landing page, the events you would measure, the review points, and the rule you would use to stop or continue. Do not invent budgets or results.
questions.answer: Treat it as a test that must earn its place against a content-and-search motion. Objective: free Blueprint starts (a lead or sales-style conversion, optimised on the free Blueprint started event once enough events exist). Landing page: the guide matching the starting point in the ad, ending in the free Blueprint. Measure: free Blueprint started and Pro upgrade by landing page, plus ad-level click-through rate, cost per Blueprint start and cost per Pro subscriber, using the pixel or Conversions API with consent. Review at 4, 8 and 12 weeks along impressions, clicks, Blueprints, Pro. Clicks without Blueprints means improve the landing page close; impressions without clicks means improve the hook. Stop or continue by comparing cost per Pro subscriber with what a subscriber pays (about £228 a year at £19 a month, before churn and costs): if acquisition costs exceed that, stop or change the offer; avoid judging before the learning phase and the early weeks have passed. Keep ads within the editorial and brand rules, advertise only features that exist, and set the budget from what the business is willing to spend rather than from this plan.
questions.rubric: A good answer: ties the test to Moksy's documented economics and motion; picks a sensible objective tied to the free Blueprint event; uses the matching guide as landing page; names the two events and consent for tracking; reviews at 4, 8 and 12 weeks with the impressions-clicks-Blueprints-Pro chain and the correct diagnosis for each break; has a stop rule comparing cost per paying subscriber with what a subscriber pays; respects the learning phase; keeps to brand and editorial rules; does not invent a budget or results. Penalise guaranteed numbers, ignoring unit economics, or advertising absent features.

items.title: Positioning: the only voice not selling the build
items.body: The SEO document's central position: every page that ranks for questions such as "how much does it cost to build an app in the UK" belongs to an agency that wants to win the build, so Moksy is the only voice in the result list not selling the build, and that neutrality is the entire advantage. It sets editorial rules: never recommend a builder, not even a sister company; ranges are labelled as ranges, and as agency marketing, and only figures that appear in a source are stated, with nothing interpolated to look precise; and every guide ends in the same place: a range is not your number, and the free Blueprint is how you get yours, which is an honest conversion because it is literally what the product does. The head term is saturated by agencies with years of links, so Moksy does not fight it. The winnable ground is the gap between "I have an idea" and "I have signed an agency": questions with high intent, weak current answers and a direct line to the product. Source: docs/SEO.md section 4.

items.title: Who Moksy is for: starting points and audiences
items.body: Moksy names six starting points for a project: a booking system, an e-commerce website, a SaaS MVP, a marketplace, a school website and a mobile app (the guides compare a mobile app with a web app). Booking system and e-commerce website guides are in wave 1 of the guides; the SaaS MVP, marketplace, school website and mobile app versus web app cost guides complete the six in wave 2. The public site's audience pages are Founders, Teams and startups, Agencies, Enterprise, Education and Public sector. The product's one-line description is: Idea in, build-ready plan out; AI structures it, vetted experts refine it. Because the guides are built around the gap between having an idea and signing an agency, ads aimed at a starting point should send people to the guide for that starting point, not to a generic page. Source: docs/SEO.md and the Moksy Lexicon.

items.title: Landing pages, calls to action and what to measure
items.body: The guides are Moksy's landing pages. Wave 1 is eight guides: the software cost hub, app development cost, booking system cost, e-commerce website cost, a software requirements document template, how to compare software development quotes, fixed price versus time and materials, and questions to ask a software agency. All are linked from /resources/guides. The one primary call to action everywhere is "Start free", and "Get my Blueprint" is used on the home form only. The document says to track free Blueprint started and Pro upgrade with the landing page as a dimension, because that is the only number that says whether a page earns its place. For paid traffic the same logic applies at ad level: a high click-through rate with few Blueprint starts points at the landing page's close; low click-through points at the ad's hook. Meta's pixel or Conversions API would be needed to measure those events, and consent rules decide whether they may fire (see facebook-marketing-titan). Source: docs/SEO.md, Moksy Lexicon C7.

items.title: Brand rules for Moksy ad creative
items.body: Moksy's brand guideline and lexicon apply to ads like any other copy. Moksy is written with a capital M; the tagline is "Turn your idea into a build-ready plan." and three older taglines are retired ("Empowering your digital transformation", "Building Future-Ready Brands", "AI requirements + expert review"). The document Moksy produces is a Blueprint and the guided conversation is a Briefing; "report", "interview" and "pillars" are retired words. The spine is Idea, Briefing, Blueprint, Review, Build. Headings and buttons use Title Case, body copy sentence case, and ALL-CAPS only through the eyebrow style. Spelling is British English. Brand orange #EF4123 is the only non-neutral action colour, with one primary action per view; status colours are for state, not decoration. Imagery is minimal and icon-led, with product and data visuals preferred over stock photography. Decorative images have empty alt text; meaningful ones have descriptive alt text. Voice is friendly, professional and confident, in plain language. Source: brand-guidelines.md and MOKSY_LEXICON.md (see moksy-brand-voice).

questions.answer: Problems: it recommends a builder (a partner studio) and breaks the neutrality rule; it states an unsourced price (£4,999); it implies Moksy builds apps, but Moksy produces a build-ready plan; ALL-CAPS headline (only the eyebrow may use capitals) and the headline is not Title Case; the button is blue and says Buy Now, but the single primary action is brand orange and the CTA is Start free; stock photography instead of minimal icon-led or product visuals; it sends everyone to the home page instead of a matching guide. Rewrite: icon-led image, headline in Title Case such as "How Much Will Your App Really Cost?", body in sentence case offering your own number in a free Blueprint, orange Start free button linking to the relevant guide.
questions.rubric: A good answer names at least five of: recommends a builder; unsourced price; implies Moksy builds the app; ALL-CAPS/casing; wrong button colour and CTA label; stock photo; wrong landing page. The rewrite should respect neutrality, avoid an invented figure, use Start free in brand orange, minimal imagery and a matching guide. Credit each correct problem with its reason.

items.title: Claims and guardrails: what you may promise
items.body: Ads are claims, so they may only describe what exists and can be evidenced. Moksy's integrations plan lists Facebook sign-in as existing but gated by environment settings, and a Facebook Page import as absent: it would use the Graph API with pages_show_list and pages_read_engagement and needs Meta's App Review, and no ad should promise it unless that has changed. Figures in ads must come from a source, as the editorial rules say. Two dated cautions come from the launch promo proposal of 13 August 2026 (a proposal, not a decision, so check whether they still hold): guest AI quotas reset when a new session is minted, so inference spend is uncapped and a public free tier gets farmed, so a guest or free offer should not be pushed with paid traffic until that is fixed; and you cannot state what a free review is worth until one price table is chosen, because two disagreed, so ads should not quote review values. Source: docs/MOKSY_INTEGRATIONS_MASTER_PLAN.md and docs/promo/LAUNCH_PROMO_SPEC.md.

questions.prompt: Your Facebook test is getting plenty of clicks but very few free Blueprint starts. A colleague suggests adding "Import your Facebook Page into Moksy" to the ad to improve results. Diagnose the problem and respond to the suggestion.
questions.answer: Clicks without Blueprints points at the landing page's close or at a mismatch between the ad's promise and the page, not at the ad's hook. Check that the ad's starting point matches the guide it links to, that the page ends in the free Blueprint close with a single Start free action, that the page loads fast, and that tracking is firing correctly with consent. I would not add the Facebook Page import line: the integrations plan lists it as absent (it would need the Graph API and Meta's App Review), so the ad would promise a feature that does not exist, which misleads people and risks the ad's policy standing. Instead test a clearer hook and a sharper close, and keep claims to what Moksy does today: a free Blueprint that gives your own number.
questions.rubric: A good answer: diagnoses clicks-without-Blueprints as a landing-page or promise-mismatch problem and lists concrete checks (match, close, speed, tracking and consent); rejects the Facebook Page import claim because it is absent per the integrations plan and would need Meta App Review; proposes legitimate tests instead. Penalise accepting the claim, blaming only the audience, or inventing results.
